The test image shows two ripe tomato fruits with circular, sunken lesions featuring dark centers and concentric rings. This is clearly a **pod/fruit** infection. From the part index, pod candidates are: Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Gray_Mold, Late_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus.

The circular, deeply sunken lesions with concentric rings and dark fungal structures in the center strongly suggest **Anthracnose**. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference confirms anthracnose: sunken, darkened lesions with concentric ring patterns on fruit. The test image shows identical characteristics on tomato fruit — circular sunken lesions, dark fungal sporulation in the center, concentric rings, and pinkish surrounding tissue (consistent with "salmon pink spore appearance").
